amc12-ahsme-1963-01.title: Plug in
amc12-ahsme-1963-01.body:
At $x=-1$ the denominator $x+1$ is $0$, so the function is undefined there and $(-1,1)$ cannot be on the graph. (The others check: $0$, $\frac{-1/2}{1/2}=-1$, $\frac{1/2}{3/2}=\frac13$, $\frac{-2}{-1}=2$.)

**Answer: (D) $(-1,1)$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-03.title: Solve
amc12-ahsme-1963-03.body:
$\frac1{x+1}=x-1$ means $(x+1)(x-1)=1$, so $x^2=2$ and $x=\pm\sqrt2$ — not among (A)–(D).

**Answer: (E) none of these**

amc12-ahsme-1963-03.title: Check the choices
amc12-ahsme-1963-03.body:
$x=0$: reciprocal of $1$ is $1\ne-1$. $x=1$: $\frac12\ne0$. $x=-1$: $\frac10$ undefined. So none of the listed values work.

**Answer: (E) none of these**

amc12-ahsme-1963-04.title: Tangent line
amc12-ahsme-1963-04.body:
The line of slope $3$ is tangent to $y=x^2$ where $2x=3$, i.e. at $\left(\frac32,\frac94\right)$. Then $k=\frac94-3\cdot\frac32=-\frac94$.

**Answer: (D) $-\frac94$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-05.title: Monotonic logarithm
amc12-ahsme-1963-05.body:
$\log_{10}x$ is defined only for $x>0$, is increasing, and equals $0$ at $x=1$. So $\log_{10}x<0$ exactly when $0<x<1$.

**Answer: (E) $0<x<1$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-06.title: Midpoint of the hypotenuse
amc12-ahsme-1963-06.body:
$C$ is the midpoint of hypotenuse $AD$, so $C$ is the circumcentre: $BC=AC=CD$. With $AB=BC$, triangle $ABC$ has $AB=BC=CA$ — it is equilateral — so $\angle DAB=60^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $60^\circ$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-07.title: Compare slopes
amc12-ahsme-1963-07.body:
Slopes: (1) $\frac23$, (2) $-\frac23$, (3) $-\frac23$, (4) $-\frac32$. Perpendicular slopes multiply to $-1$: $\frac23\cdot\left(-\frac32\right)=-1$, so (1) and (4).

**Answer: (A) (1) and (4)**

amc12-ahsme-1963-08.title: Complete the cube
amc12-ahsme-1963-08.body:
$1260=2^2\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7$. To make every exponent a multiple of $3$ we need at least $2\cdot3\cdot5^2\cdot7^2=7350$.

**Answer: (D) $7350$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-09.title: General term
amc12-ahsme-1963-09.body:
The general term is $\binom7k a^{7-k}\left(-a^{-1/2}\right)^k=(-1)^k\binom7k a^{7-\frac{3k}{2}}$. We need $7-\frac{3k}{2}=-\frac12$, so $k=5$, coefficient $-\binom75=-21$.

**Answer: (C) $-21$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-10.title: Coordinates
amc12-ahsme-1963-10.body:
Take vertices $(0,0)$ and $(a,0)$; the opposite side is $y=a$. By symmetry $P=\left(\frac a2,y\right)$. Then $d=a-y$ and $d^2=\frac{a^2}{4}+y^2$.

So $\frac{a^2}{4}+y^2=(a-y)^2$, giving $\frac{a^2}{4}=a^2-2ay$, $y=\frac{3a}{8}$, and $d=\frac{5a}{8}$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{5a}{8}$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-10.title: Right triangle
amc12-ahsme-1963-10.body:
Drop the perpendicular from $P$ to the side joining the two vertices; its foot is that side's midpoint. Its length is $a-d$, and the half-side is $\frac a2$. Pythagoras: $d^2=(a-d)^2+\frac{a^2}{4}$, so $2ad=\frac{5a^2}{4}$, $d=\frac{5a}{8}$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{5a}{8}$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-12.title: Sum directly
amc12-ahsme-1963-12.body:
We only need the coordinate sum: $(\text{sum of }P)+(\text{sum of }R)-(\text{sum of }Q)=(-5)+10-(-4)=9$.

**Answer: (E) $9$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-13.title: Factor out the smallest powers
amc12-ahsme-1963-13.body:
Let $m=\min(a,b)$ and $n=\min(c,d)$. Then
$$2^a+2^b=2^m A,\quad A=1+2^{|a-b|},\qquad 3^c+3^d=3^n B,\quad B=1+3^{|c-d|}.$$
Note $B$ is never divisible by $3$, and $A$ is odd unless $a=b$ (then $A=2$). So $2^mA=3^nB$.

- **If $n<0$:** multiply by $3^{-n}$: $3^{-n}2^mA=B$. If $m\ge0$ the left side is an integer divisible by $3$ but $B$ isn't. If $m<0$, multiply by $2^{-m}$ too: $3^{-n}A=2^{-m}B$, and again the left side is divisible by $3$ but the right side isn't. Contradiction.
- **If $n\ge0$ but $m<0$:** then $A=2^{-m}\cdot3^nB$ is even, so $a=b$ and $A=2$, giving $2^{m+1}=3^nB\ge2$. Hence $m+1\ge1$, contradicting $m<0$.

So none of $a,b,c,d$ can be negative (e.g. $2^1+2^1=3^0+3^1$ shows nonnegative solutions exist).

**Answer: (E) $0$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-14.title: Sum of roots
amc12-ahsme-1963-14.body:
The roots of the first have sum $-k$; those of the second have sum $k$. Each second root is $5$ more, so $k=-k+10$, $k=5$.

Check: $x^2+5x+6$ has roots $-2,-3$; $x^2-5x+6$ has roots $3,2$ — which are $-3+5$ and $-2+5$. ✓

**Answer: (A) $5$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-15.title: Express everything in r
amc12-ahsme-1963-15.body:
Let the inradius be $r$. The triangle's height is $3r$, so its side is $2\sqrt3 r$ and its area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot12r^2=3\sqrt3r^2$. The inscribed square has diagonal $2r$, so area $2r^2$.

Ratio $3\sqrt3:2$.

**Answer: (C) $3\sqrt3:2$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-16.title: Set up with the common difference
amc12-ahsme-1963-16.body:
Write $a=b-d$, $c=b+d$. Then
$(b-d+1)(b+d)=b^2$ gives $b+d=d^2$, and $(b-d)(b+d+2)=b^2$ gives $2b-2d=d^2$.

So $b+d=2b-2d$, i.e. $b=3d$, and then $4d=d^2$. Since $d=0$ would force $b=0$, we get $d=4$ and $b=12$.

Check: $8,12,16$; $9,12,16$ is geometric (ratio $\frac43$) and $8,12,18$ is geometric (ratio $\frac32$). ✓

**Answer: (C) $12$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-17.title: Simplify
amc12-ahsme-1963-17.body:
Multiply numerator and denominator by $(a+y)(a-y)$:
$$\frac{a(a-y)+y(a+y)}{y(a-y)-a(a+y)}=\frac{a^2+y^2}{-(a^2+y^2)}=-1,$$
valid whenever the original expression is defined, i.e. $y\ne\pm a$ (and $a^2+y^2\ne0$, automatic since $a\ne0$). So it equals $-1$ for all real $y$ except two values.

**Answer: (A) all but two real values of $y$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-18.title: EF is a diameter
amc12-ahsme-1963-18.body:
The perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre, so $EF$ is a diameter and $\angle EAF=90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle). Triangles $EUM$ and $EFA$ share the angle at $E$, and both have a right angle ($\angle EMU=\angle EAF=90^\circ$). So they are similar.

**Answer: (A) $\triangle EFA$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-19.title: Inequality
amc12-ahsme-1963-19.body:
After the first $50$, count $k$ batches of $8$. Need $\frac{49+7k}{50+8k}\ge0.9$: $49+7k\ge45+7.2k$, so $0.2k\le4$, $k\le20$. Max $n=50+160=210$.

**Answer: (B) $210$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-19.title: Count the black balls
amc12-ahsme-1963-19.body:
At most $10\%$ black. The first $50$ have $1$ black — $4$ below the allowed $5$. Each batch of $8$ has $1$ black but only allows $0.8$: it uses up $0.2$ of the slack. $4\div0.2=20$ batches, $n=50+160=210$.

**Answer: (B) $210$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-20.title: Sum the progression
amc12-ahsme-1963-20.body:
In $t$ hours the man from $S$ walks $\frac t2\left(2\cdot\frac{13}{4}+\frac{t-1}{2}\right)=3t+\frac{t^2}{4}$ miles, and the man from $R$ walks $4.5t$. So $\frac{t^2}{4}+7.5t=76$, $t^2+30t-304=0=(t-8)(t+38)$, $t=8$.

The man from $R$ has walked $36$ miles and the man from $S$ $40$ miles, so the meeting point is $40-36=4$ miles nearer $R$ than $S$.

**Answer: (D) $4$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-20.title: Hour by hour
amc12-ahsme-1963-20.body:
The man from $S$ covers $3.25, 3.75, 4.25, \ldots$; after 8 hours that is $8\cdot\frac{3.25+6.75}{2}=40$. The man from $R$ covers $8\cdot4.5=36$. $36+40=76$ ✓. Difference $40-36=4$.

**Answer: (D) $4$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-22.title: Arcs
amc12-ahsme-1963-22.body:
Arc $CA=360-120-72=168^\circ$, and $E$ is its midpoint, so arcs $CE=EA=84^\circ$.

$\angle BAC$ is inscribed in arc $BC$: $36^\circ$.

Central angle $\angle BOE$ = arc $BC$ + arc $CE$ $=72+84=156^\circ$. Triangle $OBE$ is isosceles ($OB=OE$), so $\angle OBE=\frac{180-156}{2}=12^\circ$.

Ratio $\frac{12}{36}=\frac13$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac13$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-23.title: Work backwards
amc12-ahsme-1963-23.body:
End: $(16,16,16)$. Before $C$ gave: $A$ and $B$ had half: $(8,8,32)$. Before $B$ gave: $(4,28,16)$. Before $A$ gave: $(26,14,8)$.

So $A$ started with $26$ cents.

**Answer: (B) $26$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-25.title: Congruent triangles
amc12-ahsme-1963-25.body:
The square has side $16$. Triangles $CDF$ and $CBE$ are right triangles with $CD=CB$ and $\angle DCF=\angle BCE$ (both complement $\angle FCB$). So they're congruent and $CF=CE$.

Then $[CEF]=\frac12CE^2=200$, $CE=20$, and $BE=\sqrt{20^2-16^2}=12$.

**Answer: (A) $12$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-26.title: Truth table
amc12-ahsme-1963-26.body:
The statement is $(p\Rightarrow q)\Rightarrow r$. It is true whenever $r$ is true, and also whenever $p\Rightarrow q$ is false (i.e. $p$ true, $q$ false).

(1), (2), (4) have $r$ true. (3) has $p$ true and $q$ false, so $p\Rightarrow q$ is false and the implication is true. All four.

**Answer: (E) $4$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-27.title: Add lines one at a time
amc12-ahsme-1963-27.body:
The $k$-th line crosses the previous $k-1$ lines at $k-1$ distinct points, so it is cut into $k$ pieces, each splitting a region: it adds $k$ regions. Starting from $1$ region: $1+1+2+3+4+5+6=22$.

**Answer: (C) $22$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-27.title: Formula
amc12-ahsme-1963-27.body:
$n$ lines in general position give $1+n+\binom n2$ regions: $1+6+15=22$.

**Answer: (C) $22$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-28.title: Product grows with k
amc12-ahsme-1963-28.body:
The product of the roots is $\frac k3$, increasing in $k$. Real roots require $16-12k\ge0$, i.e. $k\le\frac43$. So the maximum is at $k=\frac43$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac43$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-31.title: Parity of y
amc12-ahsme-1963-31.body:
$3y=763-2x$ is odd, so $y$ is odd; and $x\ge1$ means $3y\le761$, $y\le253$. Every odd $y$ from $1$ to $253$ gives a positive integer $x=\frac{763-3y}{2}$. That's $\frac{253+1}{2}=127$ values.

**Answer: (D) $127$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-32.title: Sum and product
amc12-ahsme-1963-32.body:
We need $x+y=\frac{a+b}{3}$ and $xy=\frac{ab}{3}$.

Since $x,y<a$: $x+y<2a$, so $\frac{a+b}{3}<2a$, i.e. $b<5a$.

For real $x,y$: $(x+y)^2\ge4xy$, so $\frac{(a+b)^2}{9}\ge\frac{4ab}{3}$, i.e. $a^2-10ab+b^2\ge0$. With $t=\frac ba>1$: $t^2-10t+1\ge0$ forces $t\ge5+2\sqrt6\approx9.9$.

But $t<5$ from the first condition. Contradiction — no such rectangle exists.

**Answer: (A) $0$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-32.title: Use the area bound
amc12-ahsme-1963-32.body:
Since $x<a$ and $y<a$, $xy<a^2$, so $\frac{ab}{3}<a^2$ and $b<3a$. Also $xy\le\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)^2=\frac{(a+b)^2}{36}$, so $12ab\le(a+b)^2$, i.e. $t^2-10t+1\ge0$ with $t=\frac ba$. For $1<t<3$, $t^2-10t+1<9-10+1=0$. Contradiction.

**Answer: (A) $0$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-33.title: Distance between parallel lines
amc12-ahsme-1963-33.body:
For $y=\frac34x+c$, the distance to the given line is $\frac{|c-6|}{\sqrt{1+\frac9{16}}}=\frac45|c-6|=4$, so $|c-6|=5$, $c=1$ or $c=11$.

**Answer: (A) $y=\frac34x+1$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-33.title: 3-4-5 triangle
amc12-ahsme-1963-33.body:
A line with slope $\frac34$ makes a 3-4-5 triangle with the vertical: moving the line vertically by $h$ moves it a perpendicular distance $\frac45h$. For distance $4$, $h=5$: intercept $6\pm5$, i.e. $1$ or $11$.

**Answer: (A) $y=\frac34x+1$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-34.title: Law of cosines
amc12-ahsme-1963-34.body:
$\cos C=\frac{3+3-c^2}{6}=1-\frac{c^2}{6}<1-\frac96=-\frac12$, so $C>120^\circ$. As $c\to3^+$, $C\to120^\circ$, so $120$ is the largest such bound.

**Answer: (B) $120^\circ$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-34.title: Isosceles triangle
amc12-ahsme-1963-34.body:
Drop the altitude from $C$: it bisects $c$, and $\sin\frac C2=\frac{c/2}{\sqrt3}>\frac{3/2}{\sqrt3}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$. So $\frac C2>60^\circ$, $C>120^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $120^\circ$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-35.title: Heron's formula
amc12-ahsme-1963-35.body:
Let the other sides be $x$ and $27-x$; $s=24$. Area$^2=24\cdot3\cdot(24-x)(x-3)=72uv$ with $u=24-x$, $v=x-3$, $u+v=21$.

$72uv=36\cdot2uv$ must be a perfect square, so $2uv$ must be a square. Trying $u=1,\ldots,10$: $2uv=40,76,108,136,160,180,196,\ldots$ — only $u=7,v=14$ gives $196=14^2$.

So the sides are $10,17,21$ (area $\sqrt{72\cdot98}=84$), and the shortest is $10$.

**Answer: (B) $10$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-35.title: Split into right triangles
amc12-ahsme-1963-35.body:
Test choice (B): sides $10,17,21$. The altitude to $21$ splits it into $6+15$ with height $8$ ($6^2+8^2=10^2$, $15^2+8^2=17^2$). Area $=\frac12\cdot21\cdot8=84$, an integer. ✓ (For example, (A) would give sides $8,19,21$ with $72\cdot5\cdot16=5760$, not a square.)

**Answer: (B) $10$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-36.title: Multiplicative factors
amc12-ahsme-1963-36.body:
A win multiplies the money by $\frac32$, a loss by $\frac12$. Multiplication is commutative, so the order doesn't matter: $64\cdot\left(\frac32\right)^3\left(\frac12\right)^3=64\cdot\frac{27}{64}=27$. A loss of $64-27=37$ dollars.

**Answer: (C) a loss of \$37**

amc12-ahsme-1963-37.title: Pair up the points
amc12-ahsme-1963-37.body:
$PP_1+PP_7\ge P_1P_7$ with equality iff $P$ is between $P_1$ and $P_7$; similarly for $(P_2,P_6)$ and $(P_3,P_5)$; and $PP_4\ge0$ with equality iff $P=P_4$. All equalities hold simultaneously exactly when $P=P_4$.

**Answer: (D) at $P_4$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-37.title: Moving P
amc12-ahsme-1963-37.body:
If $P$ moves right by a small amount, $s$ changes by (number of points to the left) $-$ (number to the right) times that amount. $s$ decreases while more points lie on the right, so it is minimized at the median point $P_4$, and any move away from $P_4$ strictly increases $s$.

**Answer: (D) at $P_4$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-38.title: Two pairs of similar triangles
amc12-ahsme-1963-38.body:
Let $k=\frac{EC}{EA}$.

$AF\parallel BC$: triangles $EAF$ and $ECB$ are similar, so $\frac{EB}{EF}=k$, $EB=32k$.

$AB\parallel CG$: triangles $EAB$ and $ECG$ are similar, so $\frac{EG}{EB}=k$, $EG=32k^2$.

Since $EG=EF-GF=8$: $32k^2=8$, $k=\frac12$, $BE=16$.

**Answer: (E) $16$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-38.title: Known identity
amc12-ahsme-1963-38.body:
The two similarities give $\frac{EG}{EB}=\frac{EB}{EF}$, so $BE^2=EG\cdot EF=8\cdot32=256$ and $BE=16$.

**Answer: (E) $16$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-39.title: Mass points
amc12-ahsme-1963-39.body:
$\frac{CD}{DB}=3$: put mass $1$ at $C$ and $3$ at $B$. $\frac{AE}{EB}=\frac32$: mass at $A$ is $\frac{2}{3}\cdot3=2$. Then $E$ has mass $2+3=5$, and on line $CE$: $\frac{CP}{PE}=\frac{5}{1}=5$.

**Answer: (D) $5$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-39.title: Menelaus
amc12-ahsme-1963-39.body:
Apply Menelaus to triangle $CEB$ with transversal $A$–$P$–$D$: $\frac{CP}{PE}\cdot\frac{EA}{AB}\cdot\frac{BD}{DC}=1$, so $\frac{CP}{PE}\cdot\frac35\cdot\frac13=1$, $\frac{CP}{PE}=5$.

**Answer: (D) $5$**

amc12-ahsme-1963-40.title: Factor the difference of cubes
amc12-ahsme-1963-40.body:
$a^3-b^3=(a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2)$ gives $a^2+ab+b^2=6$, while $(a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2=9$. Subtracting: $3ab=-3$, $ab=-1$, so $x^2-81=-1$ and $x^2=80$.

**Answer: (C) between 75 and 85**
